plan.hypothesis: H0: all group means are equal vs. H1: at least one group mean differs (omnibus test)
assumptions: Three independent groups with equal sample sizes per group (balanced design)
Homogeneity of variance (common population variance across groups)
Omnibus F-test is two-sided upper-tail test (standard for ANOVA)
scientific_notes: Eta-squared (η²) is the proportion of total variance explained by group differences
For ANOVA, eta-squared relates to the noncentrality parameter λ through: λ = n*k*η²/(1-η²), where n is per-group sample size and k is the number of groups
The F-distribution for power calculation has numerator df = k-1 and denominator df = k(n-1)
Effect size interpretation: η² = 0.06 is conventionally considered a small to medium effect (Cohen's f ≈ 0.247)

answer.summary: For a balanced one-way fixed effects ANOVA with 3 independent normal groups, common variance, and population eta-squared = 0.06, the minimum sample size to achieve 80% power at significance level α = 0.05 for the omnibus F-test is **52 participants per group** (156 total). The exact solution is 51.33 participants per group; rounding up to the nearest integer yields 52 per group with achieved power of 80.56%, which exceeds the target. The preceding integer (51 per group) yields power of 79.73%, falling short of the 80% target.
answer.method: Analytic power calculation using the F-distribution via pwr::pwr.anova.test() (R package pwr v1.3-0), which implements the noncentrality parameter method for balanced one-way ANOVA. The effect size was converted from population eta-squared (0.06) to Cohen's f (0.2526) using the standard formula f = √[η²/(1−η²)]. The test is two-sided upper-tail with numerator df = k−1 = 2 and denominator df = k(n−1) = 153 at the selected design. Sample size was determined by finding the smallest integer n such that power ≥ 0.80.
assumptions: Three independent groups with equal sample sizes per group (balanced design)
Homogeneity of variance (common population variance across all groups)
Omnibus F-test with upper-tail critical region at α = 0.05
limitations: The calculation assumes no practical constraints on recruitment or data collection; attrition was not modeled and was not requested
Effect size specification (η² = 0.06) is assumed known; sensitivity to misspecification was not explored
The analytic solution assumes adequacy of large-sample approximation at n = 52 per group; finite-sample departures from normal theory were not formally assessed
Omnibus test power does not guarantee power for post-hoc pairwise comparisons or specific contrasts
The effect size η² = 0.06 is a population parameter; sample realization may differ

k <- 3                   # Number of groups
alpha <- 0.05            # Significance level
target_power <- 0.80     # Target power
balance <- TRUE          # Balanced design

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f effect size
# Relationship: f = sqrt(eta^2 / (1 - eta^2))
cohens_f <- sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))

cat("=" %+% strrep("=", 70) %+% "=\n")

cat("=" %+% strrep("=", 70) %+% "=\n\n")

cat("  Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("  Design: Balanced (equal n per group)\n")
cat("  Test: Omnibus F-test, two-sided upper-tail\n\n")

  k = k,
  f = cohens_f,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power
)

  k = k,
  f = cohens_f,
  sig.level = alpha,
  n = n_rounded
)$power

cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")

    sig.level = alpha,
    n = n_preceding

cat("  Unit: participants_per_group\n")
